facts.reason: Lower size limit for the spill-resistant vacuum breaker is disputed between sources: IPC-lineage Table 608.1 text (IPC 2000 table reproduced by Watts; Chicago's IPC-based Table 18-29-608.1) lists ASSE 1056 at 1/4 in to 2 in, while the 2021 ICC PMG CodeNotes lists 1/2 in to 2 in. Restated so it is true under either reading; RP, DC and PVB ranges agree in all sources.

fixed.fact: In IPC 2021 Table 608.1, reduced pressure principle assemblies (ASSE 1013) and double check assemblies (ASSE 1015) are listed in sizes 3/8 in through 16 in. Pressure vacuum breakers (ASSE 1020) are listed in sizes 1/2 in through 2 in, and spill-resistant vacuum breakers (ASSE 1056) in sizes up to 2 in.
fixed.note: Sources disagree on the smallest listed SVB size (1/4 in in earlier IPC Table 608.1 text, 1/2 in in the 2021 ICC CodeNotes); confirm in the 2021 code book if a question depends on it.

facts.reason: AVB lower size limit is disputed: IPC 2000 Table 608.1 (Watts reprint) and Chicago's IPC-based table show ASSE 1001 at 1/4 in to 4 in; the 2021 ICC PMG CodeNotes shows 1/2 in to 4 in. Restated with the agreed upper limit only.

fixed.fact: Pipe-applied atmospheric vacuum breakers (ASSE 1001) are listed in IPC 2021 Table 608.1 in sizes up to 4 in, for high or low hazard, backsiphonage only. Because an AVB may not stay under continuous pressure for 12 hours or more, no shutoff valve may be placed downstream of it.
fixed.note: Sources disagree on the smallest listed AVB size (1/4 in vs 1/2 in); confirm in the 2021 code book if needed.

facts.reason: Fact is correct, but the edition-history note is wrong: the 2015 IPC already used the reorganized Chapter 9 numbering (e.g., IPC-2015 Table 915.2.2 for combination waste and vent, cited in PHCP Pros 'A cure for hyperventilation'). The old Section 916 vent sizing numbering applies to 2012 and earlier editions.

fixed.note: In the 2012 and earlier IPC, vent pipe sizing was Section 916 (Table 916.1). Chapter 9 was renumbered in the 2015 edition, so it is now 906.1 and Table 906.1, and the trap-to-vent table is 909.1.

facts.reason: Misleading by omission. Per the ICC 2021 Plumbing Venting brochure (and IPC 914.4), the relief vent is required only when the circuit-vented branch serves four or more water closets AND connects to a drainage stack that receives discharge from upper horizontal branches.

fixed.fact: A relief vent is required on a circuit-vented horizontal branch that receives four or more water closets and connects to a drainage stack that also receives soil or waste from upper horizontal branches. That relief vent may also serve as the drain for fixtures in the same branch interval, but the discharge into it is limited to 4 DFU.

facts.reason: Fact checked against the ICC 2021 Plumbing Venting brochure (Table 917.2, two water closets on a 3 in stack). The note is wrong: the brochure states the single stack vent system was introduced in the 2012 IPC, not 2015.

fixed.note: Single stack venting was introduced in the 2012 IPC (Section 917), per ICC's 2021 Plumbing Venting brochure.

facts.reason: IPC 421.3 only sets the 1-1/2 in minimum shower waste outlet; the 5.7 gpm flow threshold for a 1-1/2 in trap comes from IPC Table 709.1. Source updated.

facts.reason: The potable-source sentence is in the water supply system test section, IPC 312.5 ('The water utilized for tests shall be obtained from a potable source of supply'; retained in Ohio's amended 312.5, OAC 4101:3-3-01), not 312.1. Test values confirmed on the Philadelphia Plumbing Code testing form (working pressure water test, 50 psi air test for non-plastic piping).

fixed.fact: Under IPC 2021 312.5, the water used to test the water supply system must come from a potable source. The system is tested at not less than its working pressure with water, or, for piping other than plastic, with air at not less than 50 psi.
fixed.source: IPC 2021 312.5 (ICC 2021 IPC/UPC Essentials, Session 54; Ohio OAC 4101:3-3-01 amended 312.5 keeps the potable-source sentence)

facts.reason: Misleading by omission: IPC Table 604.4 is stricter than federal law for public lavatories (0.5 gpm non-metering, 0.25 gal per metering cycle), a commonly tested value already in the KB (FLOW-001).

fixed.fact: The federal (EPAct 1992) maximums match IPC 2021 Table 604.4 for showerheads 2.5 gpm at 80 psi, private lavatory and kitchen faucets 2.2 gpm at 60 psi, water closets 1.6 gallons per flush, and urinals 1.0 gallon per flush. The IPC is stricter for public lavatories: 0.5 gpm, or 0.25 gallon per cycle for metering faucets. Federal law still allows blowout-type water closets up to 3.5 gpf.

facts.reason: Table 308.5 footnote b requires the mid-story guide only for sizes 2 in and smaller (consistent with KB PIPE-001/PIPE-005).

fixed.fact: IPC 2021 Table 308.5: PE-RT and polypropylene (PP) pipe 1 in and smaller need horizontal support every 2.67 ft (32 in); 1-1/4 in and larger every 4 ft. Vertical support is every 10 ft, with a mid-story guide for sizes 2 in and smaller.

facts.reason: Values are right for IPC Table 308.5 (CPVC 1 in and smaller 3 ft, 1-1/4 in and larger 4 ft; same as IRC Table P2605.1), but the mid-story guide applies only to 2 in and smaller (footnote b), and the note casting doubt on the IPC row is unnecessary.

fixed.fact: IPC 2021 Table 308.5: CPVC pipe or tubing 1 in and smaller needs horizontal support every 3 ft, and CPVC 1-1/4 in and larger every 4 ft. Vertical support is every 10 ft, with a mid-story guide for sizes 2 in and smaller.
fixed.note: Same values in IRC 2021 Table P2605.1.

facts.reason: IPC Table E103.3(2) has no hose bibb row. The Louisville, CO form lists hose bibb 2.5 as an add-on row with no cold/hot split and does not cite the IPC; the Town of Eagle worksheet has no hose bibb. The 2.5 WSFU hose bibb value (1.0 each additional) is the UPC Table 610.3 value (PM Engineer, 'Fixture units: Table 610.3 Uniform Plumbing Code'; Queen Creek, AZ worksheet).

fixed.fact: Other WSFU values in IPC Table E103.3(2): drinking fountain (3/8 in valve) 0.25; water closet with flushometer tank (public or private) 2.0; laundry trays (1 to 3, private) 1.4; public bathtub 4.0; private combination fixture 3.0. The IPC table has no hose bibb row; the UPC (Table 610.3) rates a hose bibb at 2.5 WSFU and each additional one at 1.0.
fixed.source: IPC 2021 Appendix E, Table E103.3(2) (City of Louisville, CO commercial water fixture count form); UPC Table 610.3 (PM Engineer, Fixture units: Table 610.3)

facts.reason: Worked example used 2.5 WSFU hose bibbs, which are not in IPC Table E103.3(2) (that value is UPC Table 610.3). Recomputed with IPC-listed fixtures only: 7.2 + 1.4 + 1.4 + 1.4 = 11.4.

fixed.fact: Worked example (IPC Table E103.3(2), total column): a house with two private bathroom groups (flush tank, 3.6 each), a kitchen sink (1.4), a dishwasher (1.4) and a clothes washer (1.4) totals 7.2 + 1.4 + 1.4 + 1.4 = 11.4 WSFU. Hose bibbs are not listed in that table, so they are added by comparison or local rule. The total is then converted to gpm demand with Table E103.3(3).

Wrong section number and incomplete exception. In the 2018/2021 IPC, protection of potable water outlets is 608.16 (ICC 2021 CodeNotes Water Heater Safety cites 608.16.1 air gap; 2018 IPC Essentials cites Table 608.16.1), so hose connections are 608.16.4.2. The clothes washer exception applies only where backflow protection is otherwise provided or integral with the machine.

fixed.fact: Every hose-threaded outlet (sillcocks, hose bibbs, wall hydrants) must be protected by an atmospheric vacuum breaker, a pressure vacuum breaker, or a permanently attached hose connection vacuum breaker. Exceptions: water heater and boiler drain valves intended only for draining, and clothes washer supply valves where backflow protection is otherwise provided or built into the machine.
fixed.source: IPC 2021 608.16.4.2 (rule text per ICC PMG CodeNotes: Backflow Preventers, 2021; 608.16 numbering per ICC CodeNotes: Water Heater Safety, 2021, and 2018 IPC Essentials Table 608.16.1)

facts.reason: Math is right (30 x 0.433 = 13 psi), but the explanation is misleading: IPC 312.2 sets a MINIMUM 10 ft head on every joint (except the top 10 ft), not a limit, and it does not limit test sections because of base pressure.

fixed.fact: During a water test of a 30 ft tall stack filled to the top, the base fittings see 30 x 0.433 = 13 psi. IPC 312.2 only requires that every joint (except the top 10 ft) be tested under at least a 10 ft head (4.33 psi), so a full-height fill puts well over the minimum on the lowest joints.

Double counts the dishwasher: IPC Table 709.1 rates a domestic kitchen sink with a disposer, dishwasher or both at 2 DFU total (as P5-76 and KB DRAI-013 say), so a dishwasher draining through the sink adds nothing. Correct total is 19 DFU; the 3 in conclusion still holds.

fixed.fact: Residential DFU example: three bathroom groups with 1.6 gpf water closets (5 each = 15), a kitchen sink with a dishwasher draining through it (2 total) and a clothes washer (2) total 19 DFU. A 3 in building drain at 1/8 in per ft is limited to 36 DFU, so 3 in works even at the flatter slope.
fixed.note: Derived from Table 709.1 and Table 710.1(1) values. Table 709.1 rates a domestic kitchen sink with a disposer, dishwasher or both at 2 DFU.
